Subject: Post-call recap: FintechAI pricing & latency trade-offs

Hi Sarah / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

- Primary use case: real-time transaction enrichment + contextual prompts for fraud scoring (low-latency critical for frontend workflows).
- Expected traffic profile (your estimate): 100M–400M tokens/month initially, with spike patterns during end-of-day processing.
- Latency target: 95th <150ms for inline prompts; 99th ideally <300ms for heavier flows.
- Budget ballpark you mentioned on call: $10k–$35k/month.

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm target monthly token volume and percent of calls requiring streaming? (action: Sarah)
2) We’ll share a unit-economics breakdown showing $/1M tokens across hosted tiers vs Dedicated (with batch settings and streaming turned on/off). (action: Marissa + Rishi)
3) If budget aligns we’ll draft a mutual action plan and SOW. I attached a template SOW and a quick usage worksheet to capture volumes.

Attachments: usage-estimates.xlsx (xlsx) — please fill in estimated daily peak QPS and percent streaming.

Thanks — Marissa

Appreciate the details, Sarah — that helps a lot. A few clarifying points while Rishi prepares the unit-econ table: 

- For pricing modeling, can you confirm the split of token sizes per call (rough averages): short prompts ~150 tokens vs long prompts ~1k tokens and percent distribution? If you have a sample request profile that's ideal.
- Target $/1M tokens: is procurement aiming for an absolute target (e.g., "$X per 1M tokens") or a total monthly spend range only? If you have an internal target that helps us recommend tiers.

If helpful, we're going to model three scenarios:
A) Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) with streaming enabled — good for quick start, higher unit cost but no commitment.
B) Hosted + Reserved bursts (monthly commit) — middle path.
C) Dedicated Reserved capacity (monthly/annual commit) — lowest unit cost and better SLO guarantees for 99th pct latency.

Rishi will lay out the trade-offs: batch size defaults, expected latency ranges (95/99th), and how streaming and SLOs affect unit economics (i.e., smaller batches for lower latency => higher $/1M).

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Sarah — following up with the unit-economics framing and latency vs cost trade-offs (high level). I attached a quick workbook with scenario numbers. 

Key assumptions: baseline model cost on hosted tier = $0.018 per 1k tokens (example); Dedicated reserved footprint reduces per-1k token compute cost by ~40% depending on commitment and quantization.

Trade-offs:
- Batch size: larger batch sizes (16–64) increase throughput and lower $/1M tokens but increase tail latency. For your 95th <150ms target, we recommend small batching (2–8) or continuous streaming for the most latency-sensitive calls.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming keeps client-perceived latency low by returning tokens as they are generated. It slightly increases compute overhead (more frequent small work units) — expect ~10–20% higher unit cost vs fully batched non-streaming.
- SLO-driven pricing: if you need strict 99th-percentile latency guarantees (<300ms) under bursty peaks, Dedicated or a higher-priority hosted tier (SLA-backed) is recommended. That typically adds a fixed premium (e.g., +15–30%) to cover reserved capacity and priority scheduling.

Example scenario (monthly 200M tokens, 40% streaming):
- Hosted pay-as-you-go, default batching: ~$2,700/month (~$13.5/1M tokens). Latency: 95th ~250–400ms (depends on peak).
- Hosted with streaming + smaller batches: ~$3,150/month (~$15.75/1M tokens). Latency: 95th ~140–220ms.
- Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit): ~$2,100/month (~$10.5/1M tokens) with 95th <120ms and 99th ~200–250ms assuming proper autoscaling config. (Numbers illustrative; will refine with your exact profile.)

Action items from our side:
1) We'll finalize the spreadsheet with per-scenario $$ per 1M tokens and expected latency ranges.
2) Marissa will share a short M.A.P. + SOW draft if the numbers look reasonable.

If you can confirm the average token-per-call and % streaming (Sarah), we'll refine the numbers and aim to get a draft SOW into DocuSign next week.

Best — Rishi
